features.title: Write and edit notes
features.summary: Create a note, change it, add to either end of it, and delete it. Deleting moves a note to Trash, and Trash is a place you can look in and take things back out of, not a countdown.
gui: Create a note in a notebook — executed (new-note-in-notebook)
Edit and save a note — executed (edit-save)
Restore a note from Trash — executed (trash-restore)
features.surface_note: The command line writes a note and files it, and does no more than that: editing, appending and deleting happen in the GUI or over REST/MCP. `notes create` exists so a note can be the end of a pipeline.

features.title: Read a note and its structure
features.summary: Fetch a note whole, or just its body, its outline, its blocks, a line range, or an earlier revision. The structured views exist so a tool can work on part of a note without re-parsing all of it.
features.surface_note: No command line: reading a note is what the GUI and the API are for.

features.title: Search your notes
features.summary: Find notes by text, tag, notebook, date and the rest of the query language, across the library or within one note.
features.surface_note: No command line search command; `notriosctl export archive --query` applies the same language to an export instead.

features.title: Notebooks that are really saved searches
features.summary: Save a query as a notebook, so a view that would otherwise be retyped becomes something you open.
features.surface_note: Made with `notebooks create --query`, since a query notebook is a notebook whose contents are whatever matches. The GUI lists them in the sidebar and does not create them yet.

features.title: Organise notes into notebooks
features.summary: Make notebooks, nest them, move notes between them, and see what a notebook deletion would take with it before agreeing to it.
gui: Choose a notebook for a new note — executed (new-note-in-notebook)

features.title: Tag and untag a note
features.summary: Attach a tag to a note, take one off, and see what a note carries. Tags are hierarchical: `field/dusk` sits under `field`.
features.surface_note: The GUI still shows tags only as sidebar navigation and cannot add or remove one. That half of the gap v0.8 H14 found is open.

features.title: See and rename tags
features.summary: List the tags in a library, see a note's tags, and rename a whole tag hierarchy at once.
features.surface_note: The GUI shows tags as sidebar navigation and does not rename them.

features.title: Group libraries into collections
features.summary: Collections sit above notebooks and are how an import keeps its material together.
features.surface_note: No command line or GUI journey; imports set the collection with --collection.

features.title: Attach and manage files
features.summary: Add files to notes, read them back, see what references what, and find attachments nothing points at any more.
features.surface_note: No GUI journey for attachment management yet.

features.title: Bring remote images into the library
features.summary: Find images a note points at on the web, check them against the domain policy, and copy the allowed ones in so the note stops depending on somebody else's server.
features.surface_note: No GUI journey; localizing is a maintenance action rather than an editing one.

features.title: Link notes to each other
features.summary: Get a stable link to a note or one of its sections, open one, check the links in a draft before saving, and register Notrios as the handler for notrios:// links.
gui: Insert a link and check it — executed (insert-and-check-link)

features.title: See the shape of the link graph
features.summary: Look at what surrounds a note, find a path between two notes, and get a report on orphans, isolates and hubs.

features.title: Templates and tasks
features.summary: Keep note templates and make new notes from them, and see the tasks across a library.
features.surface_note: No command line or GUI journey.

features.title: Live query blocks inside a note
features.summary: Put a query in a note and have its results render where it sits.
features.surface_note: No command line; the GUI renders them in place.

features.title: Do many organiser operations at once
features.summary: Send a batch of moves, tags and notebook changes as one request, so a large reorganisation is one reviewable action.
features.surface_note: No command line or GUI journey; batching is for tools.

features.title: Import from another application
features.summary: Bring in a Joplin raw export, an Obsidian vault, a Twitter or X archive, a ChatGPT or Claude export, or a Notrios archive. Every importer dry-runs first.
features.surface_note: Not in the GUI yet. The constraint is the *browser* mode, which cannot read arbitrary local paths; the desktop app can, and native directory pickers are part of the planned client architecture. This is a gap rather than a boundary.

features.title: Export your library
features.summary: Write a portable archive of everything or a chosen subset, check one for compatibility, verify one, and restore one with an explicit intent.
features.surface_note: Not in the GUI yet. The constraint is the *browser* mode, which cannot read arbitrary local paths; the desktop app can, and native directory pickers are part of the planned client architecture. This is a gap rather than a boundary.

features.title: Back up and restore the whole library
features.summary: Take a physical snapshot of the database and its attachments, verify it, and restore it — replacing this library or adopting the snapshot as a new replica.
features.surface_note: Not in the GUI yet. The constraint is the *browser* mode, which cannot read arbitrary local paths; the desktop app can, and native directory pickers are part of the planned client architecture. This is a gap rather than a boundary.

features.title: Pair two of your own libraries
features.summary: Enrol a library for synchronization, issue a single-use code, and spend it from the other side so the two learn each other's keys.

features.title: Synchronize with a replica
features.summary: Exchange changes with a paired replica, directly over an authenticated connection or through a folder you both can reach — a second drive, or a cloud folder mapped locally.

features.title: See and end trust between replicas
features.summary: List the replicas a library trusts, revoke one's key, and retire a peer after reviewing exactly what retiring it means.

features.title: Recover a replica and resolve conflicts
features.summary: Fetch a peer-verified backup, inspect one without installing it, work through sync conflicts, and decide what a shared attachment should do.

features.title: Choose where sync keys are kept
features.summary: An installed Notrios keeps the key that protects your sync material in the operating system's credential store. Move existing keys between that and the owner-only development file, in either direction.
features.surface_note: Deliberately command line only: this item forbids a credential-management REST or MCP surface.

features.title: Watch and steer long-running work
features.summary: Imports, exports and syncs run as jobs you can list, inspect, cancel, retry and reset.
features.surface_note: No GUI journey; progress appears inline where the work was started.

features.title: Keep separate libraries
features.summary: Run more than one library on a machine — personal notes, work notes, a blog — each with its own database, its own settings and its own address.
features.surface_note: Not in the GUI yet. A profile registry is about this machine, which the desktop app also runs on, so this is a gap rather than a boundary; the browser mode is the part that genuinely cannot manage it.

features.title: Publish a subset of your notes
features.summary: Choose what leaves the library, review exactly what a publication would include and withhold, save that choice as a profile, and publish only after agreeing to the reviewed plan.
features.surface_note: Not in the GUI yet. Publishing writes to a local directory, so the desktop app could do it and the browser mode could not.

features.title: Keep a library healthy
features.summary: Find what has rotted, fix what can be fixed mechanically, reclaim space, and check that this installation is set up the way you think it is.
features.surface_note: No GUI journey; maintenance is command line work.

features.title: Move a pre-0.8 library into place
features.summary: A library that lived in ./data next to the program is relocated into the directories an installed Notrios uses, after showing you the plan.
features.surface_note: Command line only, and genuinely so: it relocates the directories the running program uses, which is not something the program can sensibly do to itself while serving them.

features.title: Let an AI assistant use your library
features.summary: Notrios speaks MCP, so an assistant can read and, within a scope you grant, change your notes.
features.surface_note: The endpoint itself has no command line or GUI; the tools it exposes are listed against the features above.
